senses.d: A person using long-range small arms for precise attacks from a concealed position.
ex: The sniper shot him in the head.

senses.d: Any attacker using a non-contact weapon against a specific target from a concealed position.
One who shoots from a concealed position.
One who criticizes; a person who frequently snipes at others.
ex: They always sniped at each other in public. German snipers were a wishy-washy lot compared with Lester and his wife.

senses.d: A player who specializes in scoring goals.
ex: Alexander Ovechkin is often regarded as the greatest sniper of his generation.

senses.d: A person or automated process set up by a person who or which attempts to win an online auction by placing a bid only seconds before the auction ends, leaving no time for other bidders to respond
ex: The smart sniper slips in and places the final winning bid when it's too late for the other bidder to respond.

ety.text: Of onomatopoeic origin, influenced by the name Cecco, nickname of Franz Joseph I of Austria during the period of the Italian irredentism.
Calque of French franc-tireur (“sniper, etc.”, literally “free-shooter”).
